Query Oracle Database as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__oracle.R
oauth_db_oracle.Rd

Open an Oracle ODBC connection with the visitor's OAuth access token. The database validates the provider's JWT and applies its configured global-user or Oracle Deep Data Security authorization model.

Usage

oauth_db_oracle(
  authorization,
  host,
  service_name,
  driver,
  ...,
  port = 1522L,
  wallet_location = NULL,
  server_cert_dn = NULL,
  authorization_model = c("global", "end_user"),
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

host

One Oracle TCPS listener hostname or IP address.

service_name

Oracle database service name, not a SID or TNS alias.

driver

Registered Oracle ODBC driver name, or its library path when supported by the driver manager. Install a client that supports the database's OAuth integration; newer integrations need a current client.

...

Result options timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, or interruptible; Oracle ODBC options FBS (fetch buffer size) and DBA ("R" for read-only, "W" for read/write) are also accepted.

port

TCPS listener port. Defaults to 1522; use the port supplied by your administrator, which may differ for self-hosted databases.

wallet_location

Optional Oracle wallet directory for TLS trust or mutual TLS. NULL uses the Oracle client's configured trust store.

server_cert_dn

Optional expected server certificate distinguished name. NULL uses Oracle's hostname matching. Certificate matching is always enabled.

authorization_model

"global" requires Oracle to report TOKEN_GLOBAL authentication, preserving the global-schema model used by existing Entra configurations. "end_user" requires Oracle Deep Data Security to expose system-managed token claims matching the submitted JWT's issuer, subject and audience. It never falls back to global-schema privileges. Use this for configured OCI IAM OAuth and Keycloak direct-logon deployments.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an odbc DBI connection.

Details

Install odbc and Oracle Instant Client's Basic and ODBC packages. The database must trust the token's provider and audience and map the visitor to a global schema or Deep Data Security data roles. Supported routes include Microsoft Entra, OCI IAM Identity Domains OAuth, and the configurable OAuth provider documented for Keycloak in Oracle 26ai. Server and client version requirements differ between these integrations; a JWT from an unconfigured provider does not establish database access. See vignette("oracle", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for sign-in setup.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each operation. Global-schema sessions survive ordinary token renewal. End-user sessions are reopened on access when the token changes, so new identity and role claims reach the database without replaying completed queries. Account changes, sign-out, permission loss and session end close the connection. A broken connection is reopened with the current token on access.

The helper builds a separate TCPS descriptor for each connection. It sets TOKEN_AUTH=OAUTH, supplies the token through a private temporary file, and removes that file on success, error or interrupt. On Windows the directory inherits R's temporary-directory access rules; run R with a private user temporary directory. Shared TNS_ADMIN, tnsnames.ora, and sqlnet.ora files are not modified.

Oracle ODBC failover is disabled because the temporary token file is removed after connection opening. Before returning a connection, the helper verifies the selected authorization model and disconnects on failure. In "end_user" mode, jsonlite is also required. Local JWT decoding identifies the expected claims; Oracle verifies the signature and establishes the system-managed context. DSNs, alternate credentials and authentication overrides cannot be supplied through ....

Scope names are checked literally, as with generic OAuth helpers. Keep Entra's /.default consent marker in the client configuration, not in this helper's required_scopes. OCI IAM proof-of-possession tokens, password authentication and application-mediated two-token contexts are separate mechanisms. For ORDS REST resources use oauth_db_oracle_ords_api().

See also

vignette("oracle", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_oracle(
  auth$connection,
  host = "database.example.org",
  service_name = "reporting.example.org",
  driver = "Oracle in instantclient_19_30"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT USER AS database_user FROM DUAL")
})
} # }
